title: Prime-chain length versus valuation rational rank
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $A$ be a valuation ring of $K$, i.e. a subring $A\subseteq K$ such that for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ lies in $A$; write $A^\times$ for its unit group. Put $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ and $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)=\dim_{\mathbf Q}(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$. If $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ are prime ideals of $A$, then $n\le\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$.

source.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 (Abhyankar inequality) and Corollary 2.1.3(i) for the height consequence; the local document copy is unavailable.
